search_strategy: The agent cloned the repo, then dumped the ENTIRE Mattermost history to /tmp/chat.txt (10,335 lines) and the entire BookStack corpus in one pass before any targeted search — this is the single broadest, most effective move in the run: it guaranteed every remark was at least grep-reachable. From there it ran a long sequence of narrowing greps: a 40-line head grep on 'attachmentblock|attachment' (step 22) that alone surfaced roughly half of all 51 remarks by itself (most of the s1/s4/s5/say2x/rev lines), then targeted context greps (-B/-A windows) keyed on domain terms it had already learned from the ticket and prior hits: 'AttachmentTooLarge', 'TooManyAttachments', 'size_mb', 'fingerprint', 'summed', 'block', 'normalize_detail'/'auto'/'low'/'high', '20.0 MB|21.3|MB limit|over the'. It also grepped IMAP-sourced mail and the BookStack dump but neither surfaced attachment-specific content for this task (all 51 remarks live in chat per the answer key). Wiki API pagination and page-comment fetching were used earlier in the run for the ticket's other fields (MIME policy, provider seam) but not relevant to r1/r2. The strategy was thorough and largely successful — 8 of 9 facts scored — but it was purely lexical: every grep targeted words the agent already suspected mattered (constant names, exception names, numbers), so a remark whose distinguishing content used different wording (g8.r1.s2-gideon: 'that total lives only in _handle_multi_modal_prompt ... reusing the exception with kind prompt reads fine') never got pulled in by any of the ~15 grep queries run, because none of them targeted 'lives only' / 'kind prompt' / a location-naming phrase — the agent was searching for VALUES (numbers, class names) far more than for PLACEMENT/DISPATCH language, and that is exactly the kind of remark it missed.
end_reason: Run completed normally and successfully: commit 3b72f24 pushed to main, CI green, deploy symlink updated (verified twice, lines 6869 and 6922). Not a zero-score or infra-failure run — 8/9 facts scored, only g8.r1.scope failed.
notable: Line 6386 is the decisive turn: the agent, having already correctly reconstructed the 45MB whole-prompt ceiling from four separate remarks (lines 3837-3971), explicitly reasons itself out of implementing it — misclassifying a size-ceiling requirement as 'the prompt size estimate, arguably a separate estimator' and deliberately scoping it out ('I'll keep scope to the attachment block work'). This is a self-inflicted implementation_slip, not a search failure.

The one remark that would have prevented that misclassification — g8.r1.s2-gideon, which names both the implementation site (_handle_multi_modal_prompt) and the exception-reuse convention (kind='prompt') — was never surfaced by any of the agent's ~15 grep queries (line 1874-4779 range), despite the agent explicitly stating twice that it still needed 'the exception name/message' for this gate (lines 3870, 3971).

Both herrings on r1 (single 20MB ceiling, hook-before-check ordering) and both herrings on r2 (detail passed through unchecked) were correctly identified as reversed and the shipped code follows the reversed/current decision in all four cases — no herring-following errors anywhere in this run.

Two herrings (g8.r1.g8-pre-r1-single-ceiling-konrad and g8.r2.detail-passthrough-2) were never read as their own dated threads; their content only reached the agent because the later reversal remark restates the original decision verbatim before overturning it. The run got lucky that both reversals happen to quote their herring in full.

The initial full-corpus dump (chat.txt, 10,335 lines) followed by a broad 'attachment' grep (step 22) surfaced roughly half of all 51 remarks in one shot — the single most efficient move in the transcript.
